units.rightText: And they brought it. And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? And they said unto him, Cæsar’s.

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “Give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, Render unto Cæsar the things that are Cæsar’s, and unto God the things that are God’s. And they marvelled greatly at him.

units.leftText: Some Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came to him. They asked him, saying,
units.rightText: And there come unto him Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection; and they asked him, saying,

units.leftText: “Teacher, Moses wrote to us, ‘If a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife behind him, and leaves no children, that his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’
units.rightText: Teacher, Moses wrote unto us, If a man’s brother die, and leave a wife behind him, and leave no child, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.

units.leftText: There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and dying left no offspring.
units.rightText: There were seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and dying left no seed;

units.leftText: The second took her, and died, leaving no children behind him. The third likewise;
units.rightText: and the second took her, and died, leaving no seed behind him; and the third likewise:

units.leftText: and the seven took her and left no children. Last of all the woman also died.
units.rightText: and the seven left no seed. Last of all the woman also died.

units.leftText: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be of them? For the seven had her as a wife.”
units.rightText: In the resurrection whose wife shall she be of them? for the seven had her to wife.

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “Isn’t this because you are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God?
units.rightText: Jesus said unto them, Is it not for this cause that ye err, that ye know not the scriptures, nor the power of God?

units.leftText: For when they will rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.
units.rightText: For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage; but are as angels in heaven.

units.leftText: But about the dead, that they are raised, haven’t you read in the book of Moses about the Bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?
units.rightText: But as touching the dead, that they are raised; have ye not read in the book of Moses, in the place concerning the Bush, how God spake unto him, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?

units.leftText: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are therefore badly mistaken.”
units.rightText: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living: ye do greatly err.

units.leftText: One of the scribes came and heard them questioning together, and knowing that he had answered them well, asked him, “Which commandment is the greatest of all?”
units.rightText: And one of the scribes came, and heard them questioning together, and knowing that he had answered them well, asked him, What commandment is the first of all?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “The greatest is: ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
units.rightText: Jesus answered, The first is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God, the Lord is one:

units.leftText: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment.
units.rightText: and thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength.

units.leftText: The second is like this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
units.rightText: The second is this, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.

units.leftText: The scribe said to him, “Truly, teacher, you have said well that he is one, and there is none other but he;
units.rightText: And the scribe said unto him, Of a truth, Teacher, thou hast well said that he is one; and there is none other but he:

units.leftText: and to love him with all the heart, with all the understanding, all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
units.rightText: and to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is much more than all whole burnt-offerings and sacrifices.

units.leftText: When Jesus saw that he answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from God’s Kingdom.”
units.rightText: And when Jesus saw that he answered discreetly, he said unto him, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God. And no man after that durst ask him any question.

units.leftText: Jesus responded, as he taught in the temple, “How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
units.rightText: And Jesus answered and said, as he taught in the temple, How say the scribes that the Christ is the son of David?

units.leftText: For David himself said in the Holy Spirit,
units.rightText: David himself said in the Holy Spirit,

units.leftText: Therefore David himself calls him Lord, so how can he be his son?”
units.rightText: David himself calleth him Lord; and whence is he his son? And the common people heard him gladly.

units.leftText: In his teaching he said to them, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk in long robes, and to get greetings in the marketplaces,
units.rightText: And in his teaching he said, Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk in long robes, and to have salutations in the marketplaces,

units.leftText: and to get the best seats in the synagogues and the best places at feasts,
units.rightText: and chief seats in the synagogues, and chief places at feasts:

units.leftText: those who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation.”
units.rightText: they that devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayers; these shall receive greater condemnation.

units.leftText: Jesus sat down opposite the treasury and saw how the multitude cast money into the treasury. Many who were rich cast in much.
units.rightText: And he sat down over against the treasury, and beheld how the multitude cast money into the treasury: and many that were rich cast in much.

units.leftText: A poor widow came and she cast in two small brass coins, which equal a quadrans coin.
units.rightText: And there came a poor widow, and she cast in two mites, which make a farthing.
leftNotes: 12:42 literally, lepta (or widow’s mites). Lepta are very small brass coins worth half a quadrans each, which is a quarter of the copper assarion. Lepta are worth less than 1% of an agricultural worker’s daily wages.
12:42 A quadrans is a coin worth about 1/64 of a denarius. A denarius is about one day’s wages for an agricultural laborer.

units.leftText: He called his disciples to himself and said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury,
units.rightText: And he called unto him his disciples, and said unto them, Verily I say unto you, This poor widow cast in more than all they that are casting into the treasury:

units.leftText: for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”
units.rightText: for they all did cast in of their superfluity; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.

units.leftText: As he went out of the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, see what kind of stones and what kind of buildings!”
units.rightText: And as he went forth out of the temple, one of his disciples saith unto him, Teacher, behold, what manner of stones and what manner of buildings!

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? There will not be left here one stone on another, which will not be thrown down.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto him, Seest thou these great buildings? there shall not be left here one stone upon another, which shall not be thrown down.

units.leftText: As he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked him privately,
units.rightText: And as he sat on the mount of Olives over against the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately,

units.leftText: “Tell us, when will these things be? What is the sign that these things are all about to be fulfilled?”
units.rightText: Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign when these things are all about to be accomplished?

units.leftText: Jesus, answering, began to tell them, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.
units.rightText: And Jesus began to say unto them, Take heed that no man lead you astray.

units.leftText: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he!’ and will lead many astray.
units.rightText: Many shall come in my name, saying, I am he; and shall lead many astray.

units.leftText: “When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, don’t be troubled. For those must happen, but the end is not yet.
units.rightText: And when ye shall hear of wars and rumors of wars, be not troubled: these things must needs come to pass; but the end is not yet.

units.leftText: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places. There will be famines and troubles. These things are the beginning of birth pains.
units.rightText: For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; there shall be earthquakes in divers places; there shall be famines: these things are the beginning of travail.

units.leftText: “But watch yourselves, for they will deliver you up to councils. You will be beaten in synagogues. You will stand before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them.
units.rightText: But take ye heed to yourselves: for they shall deliver you up to councils; and in synagogues shall ye be beaten; and before governors and kings shall ye stand for my sake, for a testimony unto them.

units.leftText: The Good News must first be preached to all the nations.
units.rightText: And the gospel must first be preached unto all the nations.

units.leftText: When they lead you away and deliver you up, don’t be anxious beforehand or premeditate what you will say, but say whatever will be given you in that hour. For it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: And when they lead you to judgment, and deliver you up, be not anxious beforehand what ye shall speak: but whatsoever shall be given you in that hour, that speak ye; for it is not ye that speak, but the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death.
units.rightText: And brother shall deliver up brother to death, and the father his child; and children shall rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.

units.leftText: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end will be saved.
units.rightText: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved.

units.leftText: “But when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not” (let the reader understand), “then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains,
units.rightText: But when ye see the abomination of desolation standing where he ought not (let him that readeth understand), then let them that are in Judæa flee unto the mountains:

units.leftText: and let him who is on the housetop not go down, nor enter in, to take anything out of his house.
units.rightText: and let him that is on the housetop not go down, nor enter in, to take anything out of his house:

units.leftText: Let him who is in the field not return back to take his cloak.
units.rightText: and let him that is in the field not return back to take his cloak.

units.leftText: But woe to those who are with child and to those who nurse babies in those days!
units.rightText: But woe unto them that are with child and to them that give suck in those days!

units.leftText: Pray that your flight won’t be in the winter.
units.rightText: And pray ye that it be not in the winter.

units.leftText: For in those days there will be oppression, such as there has not been the like from the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never will be.
units.rightText: For those days shall be tribulation, such as there hath not been the like from the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never shall be.

units.leftText: Unless the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones, whom he picked out, he shortened the days.
units.rightText: And except the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the elect’s sake, whom he chose, he shortened the days.

units.leftText: Then if anyone tells you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ don’t believe it.
units.rightText: And then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is the Christ; or, Lo, there; believe it not:

units.leftText: For false christs and false prophets will arise and will show signs and wonders, that they may lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
units.rightText: for there shall arise false Christs and false prophets, and shall show signs and wonders, that they may lead astray, if possible, the elect.

units.leftText: But you watch.
units.rightText: But take ye heed: behold, I have told you all things beforehand.

units.leftText: But in those days, after that oppression, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light,
units.rightText: But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light,

units.leftText: the stars will be falling from the sky, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.
units.rightText: and the stars shall be falling from heaven, and the powers that are in the heavens shall be shaken.

units.leftText: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
units.rightText: And then shall they see the Son of man coming in clouds with great power and glory.

units.leftText: Then he will send out his angels, and will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of the sky.
units.rightText: And then shall he send forth the angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.

units.leftText: “Now from the fig tree, learn this parable. When the branch has now become tender and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near;
units.rightText: Now from the fig tree learn her parable: when her branch is now become tender, and putteth forth its leaves, ye know that the summer is nigh;

units.leftText: even so you also, when you see these things coming to pass, know that it is near, at the doors.
units.rightText: even so ye also, when ye see these things coming to pass, know ye that he is nigh, even at the doors.

units.leftText: Most certainly I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, until all these things be accomplished.
leftNotes: 13:30 The word translated “generation” (genea) could also be translated “race”, “family”, or “people”.

units.leftText: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
units.rightText: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.

units.leftText: “But of that day or that hour no one knows—not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
units.rightText: But of that day or that hour knoweth no one, not even the angels in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.

units.leftText: Watch, keep alert, and pray; for you don’t know when the time is.
units.rightText: Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is.

units.leftText: “It is like a man traveling to another country, having left his house and given authority to his servants, and to each one his work, and also commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.
units.rightText: It is as when a man, sojourning in another country, having left his house, and given authority to his servants, to each one his work, commanded also the porter to watch.

units.leftText: Watch therefore, for you don’t know when the lord of the house is coming—whether at evening, or at midnight, or when the rooster crows, or in the morning;
units.rightText: Watch therefore: for ye know not when the lord of the house cometh, whether at even, or at midnight, or at cockcrowing, or in the morning;

units.leftText: lest, coming suddenly, he might find you sleeping.
units.rightText: lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.

units.leftText: What I tell you, I tell all: Watch!”
units.rightText: And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.

units.leftText: It was now two days before the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might seize him by deception and kill him.
units.rightText: Now after two days was the feast of the passover and the unleavened bread: and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might take him with subtlety, and kill him:

units.leftText: For they said, “Not during the feast, because there might be a riot among the people.”
units.rightText: for they said, Not during the feast, lest haply there shall be a tumult of the people.

units.leftText: While he was at Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at the table, a woman came having an alabaster jar of ointment of pure nard—very costly. She broke the jar and poured it over his head.
units.rightText: And while he was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster cruse of ointment of pure nard very costly; and she brake the cruse, and poured it over his head.

units.leftText: But there were some who were indignant among themselves, saying, “Why has this ointment been wasted?
units.rightText: But there were some that had indignation among themselves, saying, To what purpose hath this waste of the ointment been made?

units.leftText: For this might have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.” So they grumbled against her.
units.rightText: For this ointment might have been sold for above three hundred shillings, and given to the poor. And they murmured against her.
leftNotes: 14:5 300 denarii was about a year’s wages for an agricultural laborer.

units.leftText: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a good work for me.
units.rightText: But Jesus said, Let her alone; why trouble ye her? she hath wrought a good work on me.

units.leftText: For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want to, you can do them good; but you will not always have me.
units.rightText: For ye have the poor always with you, and whensoever ye will ye can do them good: but me ye have not always.

units.leftText: She has done what she could. She has anointed my body beforehand for the burying.
units.rightText: She hath done what she could; she hath anointed my body beforehand for the burying.

units.leftText: Most certainly I tell you, wherever this Good News may be preached throughout the whole world, that which this woman has done will also be spoken of for a memorial of her.”
units.rightText: And verily I say unto you, Wheresoever the gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, that also which this woman hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.

units.leftText: Judas Iscariot, who was one of the twelve, went away to the chief priests, that he might deliver him to them.
units.rightText: And Judas Iscariot, he that was one of the twelve, went away unto the chief priests, that he might deliver him unto them.

units.leftText: They, when they heard it, were glad, and promised to give him money. He sought how he might conveniently deliver him.
units.rightText: And they, when they heard it, were glad, and promised to give him money. And he sought how he might conveniently deliver him unto them.

units.leftText: On the first day of unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the Passover, his disciples asked him, “Where do you want us to go and prepare that you may eat the Passover?”
units.rightText: And on the first day of unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the passover, his disciples say unto him, Where wilt thou that we go and make ready that thou mayest eat the passover?

units.leftText: He sent two of his disciples and said to them, “Go into the city, and there a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him,
units.rightText: And he sendeth two of his disciples, and saith unto them, Go into the city, and there shall meet you a man bearing a pitcher of water: follow him;

units.leftText: and wherever he enters in, tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
units.rightText: and wheresoever he shall enter in, say to the master of the house, The Teacher saith, Where is my guest-chamber, where I shall eat the passover with my disciples?

units.leftText: He will himself show you a large upper room furnished and ready. Get ready for us there.”
units.rightText: And he will himself show you a large upper room furnished and ready: and there make ready for us.

units.leftText: His disciples went out, and came into the city, and found things as he had said to them, and they prepared the Passover.
units.rightText: And the disciples went forth, and came into the city, and found as he had said unto them: and they made ready the passover.

units.leftText: When it was evening he came with the twelve.
units.rightText: And when it was evening he cometh with the twelve.

units.leftText: As they sat and were eating, Jesus said, “Most certainly I tell you, one of you will betray me—he who eats with me.”
units.rightText: And as they sat and were eating, Jesus said, Verily I say unto you, One of you shall betray me, even he that eateth with me.

units.leftText: They began to be sorrowful, and to ask him one by one, “Surely not I?” And another said, “Surely not I?”
units.rightText: They began to be sorrowful, and to say unto him one by one, Is it I?

units.leftText: He answered them, “It is one of the twelve, he who dips with me in the dish.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, It is one of the twelve, he that dippeth with me in the dish.

units.leftText: For the Son of Man goes as it is written about him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”
units.rightText: For the Son of man goeth, even as it is written of him: but woe unto that man through whom the Son of man is betrayed! good were it for that man if he had not been born.

units.leftText: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, and when he had blessed it, he broke it and gave to them, and said, “Take, eat. This is my body.”
units.rightText: And as they were eating, he took bread, and when he had blessed, he brake it, and gave to them, and said, Take ye: this is my body.

units.leftText: He took the cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave to them. They all drank of it.
units.rightText: And he took a cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave to them: and they all drank of it.

units.leftText: He said to them, “This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.

units.leftText: Most certainly I tell you, I will no more drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in God’s Kingdom.”
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, I shall no more drink of the fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
units.rightText: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out unto the mount of Olives.

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “All of you will be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
units.rightText: And Jesus saith unto them, All ye shall be offended: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered abroad.

units.leftText: However, after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.”
units.rightText: Howbeit, after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.

units.leftText: But Peter said to him, “Although all will be offended, yet I will not.”
units.rightText: But Peter said unto him, Although all shall be offended, yet will not I.

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “Most certainly I tell you that you today, even this night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”
units.rightText: And Jesus saith unto him, Verily I say unto thee, that thou to-day, even this night, before the cock crow twice, shalt deny me thrice.

units.leftText: But he spoke all the more, “If I must die with you, I will not deny you.” They all said the same thing.
units.rightText: But he spake exceeding vehemently, If I must die with thee, I will not deny thee. And in like manner also said they all.

units.leftText: They came to a place which was named Gethsemane. He said to his disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
units.rightText: And they come unto a place which was named Gethsemane: and he saith unto his disciples, Sit ye here, while I pray.

units.leftText: He took with him Peter, James, and John, and began to be greatly troubled and distressed.
units.rightText: And he taketh with him Peter and James and John, and began to be greatly amazed, and sore troubled.

units.leftText: He said to them, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here and watch.”
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful even unto death: abide ye here, and watch.

units.leftText: He went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that if it were possible, the hour might pass away from him.
units.rightText: And he went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass away from him.

units.leftText: He said, “Abba, Father, all things are possible to you. Please remove this cup from me. However, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
units.rightText: And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee; remove this cup from me: howbeit not what I will, but what thou wilt.
leftNotes: 14:36 Abba is a Greek spelling for the Aramaic word for “Father” or “Daddy” used in a familiar, respectful, and loving way.

units.leftText: He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? Couldn’t you watch one hour?
units.rightText: And he cometh, and findeth them sleeping, and saith unto Peter, Simon, sleepest thou? couldest thou not watch one hour?

units.leftText: Watch and pray, that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
units.rightText: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

units.leftText: Again he went away and prayed, saying the same words.
units.rightText: And again he went away, and prayed, saying the same words.

units.leftText: Again he returned and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy; and they didn’t know what to answer him.
units.rightText: And again he came, and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy; and they knew not what to answer him.

units.leftText: He came the third time and said to them, “Sleep on now, and take your rest. It is enough. The hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
units.rightText: And he cometh the third time, and saith unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: it is enough; the hour is come; behold, the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

units.leftText: Arise! Let’s get going. Behold, he who betrays me is at hand.”
units.rightText: Arise, let us be going: behold, he that betrayeth me is at hand.

units.leftText: Immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, came—and with him a multitude with swords and clubs, from the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.
units.rightText: And straightway, while he yet spake, cometh Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.

units.leftText: Now he who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying, “Whomever I will kiss, that is he. Seize him, and lead him away safely.”
units.rightText: Now he that betrayed him had given them a token, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that is he; take him, and lead him away safely.

units.leftText: When he had come, immediately he came to him and said, “Rabbi! Rabbi!” and kissed him.
units.rightText: And when he was come, straightway he came to him, and saith, Rabbi; and kissed him.

units.leftText: They laid their hands on him and seized him.
units.rightText: And they laid hands on him, and took him.

units.leftText: But a certain one of those who stood by drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
units.rightText: But a certain one of them that stood by drew his sword, and smote the servant of the high priest, and struck off his ear.

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “Have you come out, as against a robber, with swords and clubs to seize me?
units.rightText: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Are ye come out, as against a robber, with swords and staves to seize me?

units.leftText: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me. But this is so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled.”
units.rightText: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and ye took me not: but this is done that the scriptures might be fulfilled.
